content.text: Tylenol’s met intermed = detoxified by glutathione
•poisoning common in small children exploring their environment; APAP = common accidental agent
▪︎also via iatrogenic IV overdose or caregiver inappropriate dosing
Recommended peds dose 10-15 mg/kg/dose, ⍉to exceed 90 mg/kg/d for >1 day
→ fulminant hepatic necrosis w/ jaundice, hepatic encephalopathy, AKI, death
Course: 0-24hrs Sx mild or ⍉existent; 24-72hrs liver toxicity (RUQ pain, ⇡ liver enzymes, ⇡ PT); days 3-4 liver failure & multiorgan failure (pt most likely to die); days 4-14 recovery, liver heals
Prognosis excellent in children <5yo w/ accidental toxic ingestion & prompt care
▪︎level ≥4hrs after ingestion, then q1-2hrs to plot elimination during tx
Activated charcoal 1 g/kg if known dose >150 mg/kg & within 4hrs of presentation
▪︎charcoal CI: intestinal obstruction, AMS w/o protected airway
▪︎emergent care if dose >200 mg/kg or 10g total (whichever less) in 24hrs, unknown amt ingested, or signs of toxicity
▪︎gastric lavage ⍉routine (risks > benefits); Mg citrate outdated & ⍉in children; syrup of ipecac no longer advised
Prevention: careful storage of meds & strict attention to recommended dosing
Single ingestion > 200 mg/kg = likely to cause sig acute intoxication
100% O2 by tight-fitting ↑flow reservoir face mask or ET tube
: Warfarin, “superwarfarins”, direct thrombin inhibitors, Xa inhibitors
Rodenticides; effects can last for wks or months
Vit K (if PT ↑), FFP, PCC, or activated factor 7 if needed
Oxidation of ferrous Hgb to its ferric state (methemoglobin)
: Benzocaine, propanil (herbicide), nitrites, nitrogen oxide gas, dapsone, phenazopyridine
•Rapidly absorbed by inhalation, skin absorb, ingestion
HA, dizziness nausea, abd pain, anxiety
→ confusion, syncope, shock, seizures, coma, death
- if from nitroprusside infusion, slow or stop med
